questions.q: Cyclohexanone is converted into its pyrrolidine enamine, which is treated with methyl vinyl ketone and then dilute H₃O⁺. The product is:
questions.explain: The enamine α-carbon adds to the β-carbon of the Michael acceptor, and hydrolysis removes the amine, giving a 1,5-diketone.

questions.q: Which amine is used to make an enamine from a ketone?
questions.explain: Secondary amines (pyrrolidine, piperidine, morpholine) give enamines; primary amines such as methanamine or aniline give imines, and tertiary amines do not condense with C=O.

questions.q: The pyrrolidine enamine of cyclohexanone is treated with an acyl chloride and then hydrolysed. The product is:
questions.explain: In Stork acylation the acyl group attaches to the α-carbon, so hydrolysis gives a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound.

questions.q: Why do simple primary alkyl halides such as CH₃I often give poor yields of C-alkylated ketone in the Stork reaction?
options: The enamine is not nucleophilic at carbon
Enamines are also nucleophilic at nitrogen, and such halides often attack N first
CH₃I acts only as a Michael acceptor
questions.explain: N-alkylation competes, so the method works best with Michael acceptors and very reactive (benzylic, allylic, α-halo carbonyl) halides.
